item.title: HP CEO Enrique Lores leaves to lead PayPal

item.description: In December, Mozilla CEO Anthony Enzor-DeMeo attracted a lot of attention by announcing that Firefox would become a “modern AI browser.” In order not to alienate users, the company also promised a new setting that would make it possible to turn off some or all of the AI features, including the chatbot in the sidebar, automatic translations, tab grouping, and link previews. item.description: Intel is making a new push into GPUs, this time with a focus on data center workloads, as the chipmaker looks to reestablish itself in a market increasingly shaped by AI-driven demand and dominated by Nvidia. item.title: Amid AI gloom and doom, WEF attendees were bullish on physical AI
item.description: The tech bigwigs and economists at the recent World Economic Forum (WEF) in Davos were clear-eyed about how AI is reshuffling the jobs landscape globally and disrupting national economies. But the chatter around physical AI and robotics was more upbeat, with attendees saying robots with brains and intelligent sensors are likely to improve human productivity and manufacturing output.
